verses.1: In the beginning, there was the Word. And the Word was toward God. And the Word became God.
verses.2: He was at first close to the god.
verses.3: Everything happened through him; nothing could happen without him. What happened…
verses.4: In it was life, and that life was the light of human beings.
verses.5: And light appears in darkness; yet, darkness does not extinguish it.
verses.6: A man was sent by God; his name was John.
verses.7: He came to give testimony regarding the light; so that everyone might believe through him.
verses.8: That light wasn’t meant to be seen; rather, it was meant to serve as a witness regarding the nature of light itself.
verses.9: It was the true light that illuminates every person who comes into the world.
verses.10: He existed in the world, and the world was created through him. But the world did not know him.
verses.11: He came directly to them, but the people there did not receive him.
verses.12: And those who received it, they were given the authority to become children of God. They believed in His name.
verses.13: They were not created from the blood, nor from human will or desire; they were created by God alone.
verses.14: And his word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, a glory that was unique among all parents, full of grace and truth.
verses.15: John also testified about him, saying, “This man was the one who came back to me. He appeared before me as my former friend.”
verses.16: Because from his payment, we all receive something in return. And it’s a gift, not something that needs to be paid for.
verses.17: Because the law was given through Moses, but the grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
verses.18: No one ever saw a god like that. It was a single god who came into the womb of his father and explained everything there.
verses.19: And this is also the testimony of John, when the Jewish priests and Levites were sent from Jerusalem to ask him questions. Who are you?
verses.20: And he also admitted it, and refused not to do so. He also admitted that I was not the Christ.
verses.21: And they asked him, “Then who are you? Are you Elijah?” He replied, “No, I am not.” “Are you a prophet?” He answered, “Yes.”
verses.22: So they said to him, “Who are you? Let us ask those who sent us to speak with you. What do you have to say about yourself?”
verses.23: He said, “I am the voice of the warrior in the wilderness.” Go along the path of the Lord, as Isaiah the prophet said.
verses.24: And they were also sent by the Pharisees.
verses.25: And they asked him, saying, “What is it that you do, if you are not the Christ, nor the prophet?”
verses.26: John replied to them, “I baptize in water. But among you there will be one whom you do not know.”
verses.27: He who comes towards me from behind… I am not worthy of breaking off the hem of his garment.
verses.28: These things happened in Bethany, beyond the Jordan River, where John was baptizing.
verses.29: In the evening, Jesus comes towards him. He says, “Look, I am the memory of God, who forgives the sins of the world.”
verses.30: This is him, as I said. A man who came after me; he was my predecessor.
verses.31: I don’t know him personally, but it’s for Israel’s sake that I came here to baptize in water.
verses.32: And John testified that the spirit of God descended like a dove from heaven upon him.
verses.33: I do not know him. But the one who sent me to be baptized in water said to me, “If you see a spirit descending and staying over him, then this person is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.”
verses.34: I saw it, and I testified that this is indeed the chosen one of God.
verses.35: In the evening, John again appeared, along with two of his disciples.
verses.36: And when you looked at Jesus as he walked along, he said, “Look, this is the memory of the God.”
verses.37: And the two disciples heard him speaking, and they followed Jesus.
verses.38: And Jesus, seeing them following him, said to them, “What do you seek?” They replied, “Rabbi, where do you stay?”
verses.39: He said to them, “Come and see.” So they came and saw where he stayed. They spent the entire day with him there. It was about ten o’clock at that time.
verses.40: Andreas, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two men who listened to John and followed him.
verses.41: First, he finds his brother, Simon, and says to him: “We have found Messias” (which is what Christ is called in other translations).
verses.42: He brought him before Jesus. When Jesus looked at him, he said, “You are Simon, the son of John. You shall be called Kefas” (which is interpreted as Peter).
verses.43: In the evening, he decided to go to Galilee. There, he found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.”
verses.44: Philip was from Bethsaida, from the city of Andrea and Peter.
verses.45: Philip found Nathaniel and said to him, “What did Moses write in the law? And what did we find from the prophets? It is about Jesus, son of Joseph, who came from Nazareth.”
verses.46: And Nathanael said to him, “Is there anything good in Nazareth?” Philip replied to him, “Come and see for yourself.”
verses.47: Jesus saw Nadab approaching him and said something about him. “Look, truly, this is an Israelite who has no sin.”
verses.48: Nathanael said to him, “Where do you get this from?” Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
verses.49: Nathan said to him, “Rabbbi, you are the son of God, and you are the king of Israel.”
verses.50: Jesus replied to him, “Do you really think that I saw you under the fig tree? I’ve seen much more than that.”
verses.51: And he said to him, “Yes, I tell you, you will see the heavens opening up, and the angels of God going up and down to the son of man.”
